lines.trans: Wooden laundry clothespins, Tariq?! We are hosting an anniversary tea, not drying bedsheets!
Wait a second, Mazen—look how smooth and clean this natural birch wood is!
Watch what happens when I write Number One in dark carpenter pencil along the flat side.
Pencil on bare wood never smudges in water AND clips tight onto a folded cloth napkin!
Hold on... number on one side, guest name on the other side, clipped to heavy linen?!
And everyone can clip their wooden clothespin onto a saucer or pocket as a keepsake!
Tariq, Nour—that is charming, rustic, windproof, AND costs zero extra coins!
Plus I kept a full backup seat list written neatly on page forty of my ledger.
Read the names out in order, Mazen, while I letter clothespins one through twenty-eight!
Pin Number One: Our Honoured Mapmaker from Room Eight! Pin Number Two: Suad!
Look how fast Nour writes—half the street is already pinned in neat wooden rows.
Take this basket outside and test our windproof tables against the afternoon breeze!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (باخد, بياخد).

examples.trans: Someone took my suitcase by mistake!
Old buildings take time to warm up.

meanings.note: Numeral 'forty'.

examples.trans: The bus arrives in forty minutes.
I do not wear size forty-four!

meanings.note: Polite Jordanian title for any man ('sir / Mr') as well as 'teacher' or 'professor'.

examples.trans: Please have a seat, sir.
Good morning, gentlemen.

meanings.note: First person singular pronoun.

examples.trans: I am Nour, the new receptionist.
I am Salma from the kitchen.

meanings.note: Conjunction 'or' in statements and open questions.

examples.text: مكتوب عليها اسم أو رقم تليفون؟
examples.trans: Is there a name or phone number written on it?
We need two or three minutes.

meanings.note: Often placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'spare' (مفتاح احتياط a spare key).

examples.trans: I have a spare key in the drawer.
We bought a spare valve for winter.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for a person's or place's name; takes possessive endings directly (اسمي my name, اسمك your name).

examples.trans: What is your kind name?
My name is written here in the notebook.

meanings.note: Jordanian and Levantine 'for free', built from ب + بلاش ('with nothing').

examples.trans: Tea is free with breakfast.
I got the chair for free from the neighbours.

meanings.note: Used as a material noun after خشب ('birch wood') or ملقط ('birch clothespin').

examples.trans: Birch wood is smooth and light in colour.
We have clean birch clothespins.

meanings.note: Refers to being outdoors or outside a specific location.

examples.trans: It is raining outside.
A yellow taxi stopped outside the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: بسيطة, plural: بسيطين).

examples.trans: Explain the matter to me in simple words.
The problem is minor and easy to fix.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Verbal noun of رتّب ('to tidy, arrange'); بترتيب means 'neatly, in neat order'.

examples.trans: We lined the chairs up neatly beside the wall.

examples.text: ترتيب الطاولات بالساحة ما أخد عشر دقايق.
examples.trans: Arranging the tables in the courtyard did not take ten minutes.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تقيلة, plural: تقال).

examples.trans: This suitcase is very heavy today.
Take off your heavy coat and sit down to rest.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ثابتة, plural: ثابتين).

examples.trans: Hold the torch steady on the pipe.
The flame's color is steady blue.

meanings.note: Feminine plural جامدات also appears in Jordanian speech for firm fruit (متل ليمونات جامدات).

examples.text: نقي ليمونات صفر وجامدات عشان تارت الليمون.
examples.trans: Pick firm yellow lemons for the lemon tarts.

examples.text: الكريمة بردت بالبراد وصارت جامدة ومتماسكة.
examples.trans: The curd chilled in the fridge and turned firm and set.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بجرب, بيجرب).

examples.trans: This sweater is clean and new — try it on.
We tried the new recipe and it turned out delicious.

meanings.note: Used with right and left: الجهة اليمين 'the right side', من هاي الجهة 'from this side'.

examples.trans: The kitchen is on the other side.
Walk this way, it is closer.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: جيب.

examples.trans: Put the key in the coat pocket.
The paper is in my right pocket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: حفلات.

examples.trans: He designs concert halls.
We attended a lovely music concert.

meanings.note: One of the most frequently used adjectives in Jordanian Arabic to mean beautiful, sweet, nice, or good.

examples.trans: The strawberry jam is sweet and tasty.
The sweater looks lovely and warm.

meanings.note: Standard word for a geographical or digital map.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: دفاتر.

examples.trans: We wrote the name in the booking ledger.
I forgot my leather notebook on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: ذكريات.

examples.trans: This house is full of sweet memories.
Childhood memories are never forgotten.

meanings.note: Intensive occupation noun from رسم ('draw/paint'). رسام خرايط means 'mapmaker/cartographer'.

examples.text: ضيف غرفة تمانية رسام خرايط مشهور.
examples.trans: The Room Eight guest is a famous mapmaker.
The artist paints with watercolours.

meanings.note: Can mean the metal lead, or bullets. Often used in 'qalam rSaaS' (pencil).

examples.trans: We write bookings in pencil.
The name is written in pencil underneath.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Form II verb derived from رقم ('number').

examples.text: نور عم ترقم الملاقط بقلم رصاص.
examples.trans: Nour is numbering the clothespins with a pencil.

examples.text: رقمنا كل الطاولات من واحد لتمانية.
examples.trans: We numbered all the tables from one to eight.

meanings.note: Placed directly after a noun in Jordanian to mean 'extra' (قطع زيادة extra pieces, الدرج الزيادة the extra stairs).

examples.trans: I brought two extra chairs for the courtyard.
I put a little extra mint in the tea.

meanings.note: Hollow verb (يسيح / بيسيح). Used for ice melting, chocolate softening, or ink smearing in water.

examples.text: حبر القلم بيسيح إذا اجت عليه مي.
examples.trans: Pen ink runs if water gets on it.
The butter melted in the hot pan.

meanings.en: plain; solid-coloured; without pattern or sugar
meanings.note: Invariable adjective used after nouns for plain paper, fabric, or unsweetened coffee (قهوة سادة).

examples.text: جبت ورق سادة عشان الرسم يبين.
examples.trans: I brought plain paper so the drawing shows clearly.

examples.text: بدي فنجان قهوة سادة لو سمحت.
examples.trans: I'd like a cup of plain black coffee, please.

meanings.note: Respectful and warm Levantine title for a woman ('Madam / Mrs. / lady').

examples.text: يسلموا إيديكي يا ست سعاد عاللحن الحلو.
examples.trans: Bless your hands, Madam Suad, for the lovely melody.

examples.text: كل ست وشيخ بالحارة معزومين عالافتتاح.
examples.trans: Every lady and elder on the lane is invited to the opening.

meanings.note: With ب- forms the very common adverb بسرعة ('quickly / fast').

examples.trans: I always walk fast in the morning.
Your quick wit saved the day!

meanings.note: Core word in مع السلامة! ('goodbye!', literally 'with safety') and الحمد لله عالسلامة ('glad you arrived safely').

examples.trans: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
Thank goodness for your safe arrival.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: سلال.

examples.trans: I put the yellow lemons in the basket.
He tossed the paper into the wastebasket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: سنوية, plural: سنويين).

examples.trans: He writes in the annual Amman tourist guide.

examples.text: عندنا صيانة سنوية للسخان قبل الشتا.
examples.trans: We do annual maintenance on the heater before winter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شوارع.

examples.trans: Our guesthouse is on a quiet street in central Amman.
There are old stone streets in the quarter.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: A staple beverage in Jordanian culture, typically served with mint or sage.

examples.trans: Please have a glass of hot mint tea.
There is black tea and coffee at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: شراشف.

examples.trans: We spread a clean white cloth on the table.
I brought fresh sheets from the closet.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Very common adverb in Jordanian Arabic for 'a little bit' or 'slowly'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
Turn the valve slowly and gently.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بصير, بيصير).

examples.trans: You became one of us quickly!
Did the water upstairs turn cold?

meanings.note: Everyday word for both a dinner plate and a teacup saucer (صحن الفنجان).

examples.text: رتبت سلمى اتنعش صحن أبيض جنب الفناجين.
examples.trans: Salma arranged twelve white saucers next to the cups.

examples.text: حطي الكيك السخن بصحن كبير عالطاولة.
examples.trans: Put the warm cake on a big plate on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صفوف.

examples.trans: We sat in the front row at the concert.
The chairs are arranged in two rows.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: صفحات.

examples.trans: Read the second page of the letter.
The notebook fell open to the middle page.

meanings.note: Preposition meaning 'against' or 'resistant to / -proof' (ضد المي 'waterproof', ضد الهوا 'windproof').

examples.text: القارب ماشي ضد الريح بس ثابت.
examples.trans: The boat is moving against the wind yet steady.

examples.text: ما عندي شي ضد الفكرة هاي.
examples.trans: I have nothing against this idea.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun (feminine: ضيفة). Plural: ضيوف.

examples.trans: The guests are coming down to breakfast now.
We welcomed every guest with a smile.

meanings.note: Common everyday word for table.

examples.trans: We set four tables in the courtyard.
Breakfast is ready on the table.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: طبيعية, plural: طبيعيين).

examples.trans: Great service is a natural thing at our inn.
Natural juice without sugar.

meanings.note: The number twenty.

examples.trans: We need twenty eggs for breakfast.
The ring's width is twenty millimetres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: عصور.

examples.trans: We arrived at the guesthouse Monday afternoon.
Late-afternoon tea in the courtyard is a daily ritual.

meanings.note: Standard preposition for 'on', 'upon', or 'to'.

examples.trans: Your glasses are on your forehead!
Say hello to Salma for me!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بعلق, بيعلق).

examples.trans: Where should I hang this round mirror?
We hung the lanterns in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Levantine progressive marker placed before a present-tense verb to show action happening right now.

examples.trans: The water is flowing inside the pipe right now!

examples.text: كنت عم بدور على دفتري هلا.
examples.trans: I was just looking for my notebook.

meanings.note: Arabic expresses age with عمر + possessive suffix: عمره تمانين سنة ('its/his age is eighty years').

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
He has lived in this quarter all his life.

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: غامقة, plural: غامقين).

examples.trans: The suitcase's color is dark blue.
A dark grey wool coat.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: The clean sheets are in the linen closet.
We hung the laundry in the morning sun.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: فوط.

examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water.
She wiped the table with a damp cloth.

meanings.note: A written list or a restaurant menu; with -i it is قائمتي, 'my list'.

examples.trans: I wrote the shopping list before the market.
May I have the menu?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for 'in front of, before'.

examples.trans: The golden lanterns against the evening sky.
The car is parked in front of the gate.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقدر, بيقدر).

examples.text: بنقدر نقدم زبدة مالحة مع المربى؟
examples.trans: Can we serve salted butter with jam?

examples.text: ليش ما قدرت تعطيه القطار بإيدك؟
examples.trans: Why could you not hand him the train yourself?

meanings.note: The primary interrogative word for quantity, price, or duration in Levantine Arabic.

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
Look how peaceful the sky is!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قروش.

examples.trans: The bill is exact to the last piastre.
A dinar has one hundred piastres.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: قعدات.

examples.trans: Sitting in the courtyard under the tree is cosy.

examples.text: قعدة الصبح مع القهوة ما بتتعوض.
examples.trans: A morning sit-down with coffee is priceless.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun; قلم رصاص means 'pencil'. Plural: أقلام.

examples.trans: I found my pen in the jacket pocket.
We write the names with a pencil.

meanings.note: Any fabric; سلك قماش is old cloth-covered electrical wire.

examples.trans: She bought blue fabric for the curtains.
This fabric is very soft.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: كاملة, plural: كاملين).

examples.trans: He hired her for a full-time job at the guesthouse.
They stayed with us a full week.

meanings.note: Masculine material noun used both for woven linen fabric and flax/linen twine.

examples.text: هاد المريول مصنوع من قماش الكتان البارد.
examples.trans: This apron is made from cool linen fabric.
Linen holds up well in summer and its heat.

meanings.note: Depending on vowels, it means 'he wrote' (katab) or plural 'books' (kutub).

examples.text: رح يكتب تقييم حلو عن النزل.
examples.trans: He will write a lovely review of the guesthouse.
I wrote my name and number on the card.

meanings.note: A highly versatile quantifier used to mean 'all of', 'every', or 'the whole'.

examples.trans: Tell me everything I need to know.
Everyone is happy in the courtyard today.

meanings.en: to cost (money or effort); to assign someone a duty
meanings.note: Form II verb (بكلّف / كلّف). Can take two objects: هالحبل ما بكلّف كتير ('this rope doesn't cost much').

examples.trans: How much did this big lantern cost you?
City Hall tasked us with preparing the garden for the show.

meanings.note: Indispensable Levantine and Egyptian particle meaning 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.

examples.text: التفكير السريع أنقذ الفطور كمان مرة!
examples.trans: Quick thinking saved breakfast once again!
And I missed you too.

meanings.note: Common conjunction used to introduce a time clause, distinct from the question word 'when' (mita).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Used to describe a neat person, a well-organized room, or generally something of high quality (e.g. 'a nice car').

examples.trans: I recognized your neat handwriting right away.
Neat pencil sketches.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of رقّم ('to number'): feminine مرقمة, plural مرقمين.

examples.text: الأوراق مرقمة من واحد لعشرة بالترتيب.
examples.trans: The sheets are numbered from one to ten in order.
I found the numbered boxes next to the door.

meanings.note: Used for flat surfaces like roofs or fields.

examples.text: افرد الورقة على مكان مسطح قبل التلوين.
examples.trans: Spread the sheet on a flat surface before painting.
The roof here is level and suitable for the tables.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسك, بيمسك).

examples.trans: Hold this torch steady right here.
Grab the boxes, Tariq!

meanings.note: The most common negation particle in Levantine Arabic for non-verbs.

examples.trans: This is not my suitcase!
Not bad for a second day at work!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مشبوكة, plural: مشبوكين).

examples.text: في صفحة تانية مشبوكة ورا الرسالة.
examples.trans: There is a second page clipped behind the letter.
The lamp is plugged in.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مطوية, plural: مطويين).

examples.trans: We found an old folded map in the box.

examples.text: في ورقة تانية مطوية ورا الإشعار.
examples.trans: There is a second folded sheet behind the notice.

meanings.note: Everyday preposition 'with'; takes pronoun suffixes to express 'have on one's person' (معي 'I have with me', معك حق 'you are right').

examples.trans: You are right, Nour!
Goodbye! (lit. go with safety)

meanings.note: Often used as a noun meaning 'letter' (mail) or 'destiny' in traditional contexts.

examples.trans: What is written in the letter, Nour?
Our two names are still written in pencil.

meanings.note: Form II passive participle of كرّم ('to honour'): الضيوف المكرمين ('the honoured guests').

examples.trans: Welcome to our honoured guests on the rooftop terrace!
This area is reserved for honoured visitors.

meanings.note: Fine tweezers for delicate repair work, or small kitchen tongs.

examples.text: طارق طلب ملقط رفيع عشان يمسك الدبوس النحاس.
examples.trans: Tariq asked for thin tweezers to hold the tiny brass pin.

examples.text: البرغي الصغير ما بينمسك إلا بملقط.
examples.trans: That tiny screw can only be picked up with tweezers.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Universal Jordanian/Levantine word for water (feminine!). Before another noun in possession ('water of...'), becomes مية (mayyet): مية الدوش ('shower water'), مية الشتا ('winter water').

examples.trans: Please drink a glass of cold water.
The hot water is working again in the bathroom.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ناعمة, plural: ناعمين); سكر ناعم means 'powdered sugar'.

examples.trans: I brought two soft pillows for the attic.
Lemon cake dusted with powdered sugar.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: نجارين.

examples.text: النجار صنع الطاولة من خشب بلوط.
examples.trans: The carpenter built the table out of oak wood.
My grandfather was a master carpenter in the quarter.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (plural نسمات / أنسام) for a pleasant light breeze, especially in the evening.

examples.text: في نسيم بارد لطيف عالسطح بالليل.
examples.trans: There is a pleasant cool breeze on the roof at night.
The sea breeze moved the lanterns gently.

نشر.gloss: to spread out; hang out (laundry/lanterns); publish

meanings.en: to spread out to dry; hang along a line; publish
meanings.note: Form I verb (بنشر / نشر). Classic Levantine verb for hanging laundry or paper decorations along a rope.

examples.text: نشرنا الفوانيس على طول الحبل بين العواميد.
examples.trans: We hung the lanterns along the length of the rope between the posts.
My mother hung the laundry out on the roof in the morning.

meanings.note: Extremely common word used in time (e.g., 3 and a half) and measurements.

examples.trans: Breakfast starts at seven thirty.

examples.text: بس نص كاسة عصير لو سمحت.
examples.trans: Just half a glass of juice, please.

meanings.note: Natural spoken Levantine pronunciation of نظيف ('clean'), broken plural نضاف.

examples.text: مسحنا الفرشاية بقماشة نضيفة ومي دافية.
examples.trans: We wiped the brush with a clean cloth and warm water.

examples.text: المطبخ صار نضيف ومرتب وجاهز لبكرا الصبح.
examples.trans: The kitchen is spotless, tidy, and ready for tomorrow morning.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun.

examples.trans: A little air got into the old pipes.
Morning air in Amman is crisp and clean.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!
